questions.stem: Which of the following is true when two lines are parallel?
choices: They intersect at exactly one point.
questions.solution: When two lines are parallel, they never meet. This is a basic property of parallel lines. The other options are incorrect because parallel lines do not meet at any point, they have the same slope, and they intersect at only one point if they are not parallel.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes two lines that never meet, even when extended?
questions.solution: Parallel lines are defined as lines that lie on the same plane and never meet, even when extended infinitely in both directions. Intersecting lines meet at a point, perpendicular lines meet at a right angle, and skew lines are not on the same plane and do not intersect. Hence, the correct answer is parallel lines.

questions.stem: In the given figure, if line l is parallel to line m, and line n is a transversal intersecting them, which of the following is true?
questions.solution: When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal. This is a fundamental property of parallel lines and transversals. The other options are incorrect because alternate interior angles are equal, not supplementary, consecutive interior angles are supplementary, and vertical angles are equal, not complementary.

questions.stem: If a transversal intersects two parallel lines and forms corresponding angles, what can be said about these corresponding angles?
questions.solution: Corresponding angles formed by a transversal intersecting two parallel lines are always equal due to the geometric properties of parallel lines. Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees, and complementary angles add up to 90 degrees, neither of which is a requirement for corresponding angles. Different angles would not maintain the parallel relationship between the lines.

questions.stem: In a diagram, two lines intersect and form four angles. If one angle is 135°, what is the measure of the angle adjacent to it?
questions.solution: Adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines are called linear pairs and always add up to 180°. If one angle is 135°, the adjacent angle will be 180° - 135° = 45°. The other options are incorrect because 135° is the vertically opposite angle, 90° is a right angle, and 180° is a straight angle.

questions.stem: In the given figure, line a is parallel to line c. If ∠1 = 52°, what is the value of ∠2?
questions.solution: Since line a is parallel to line c and a transversal intersects them, ∠1 and ∠2 are consecutive interior angles. According to the property, consecutive interior angles add up to 180°. If ∠1 is 52°, then ∠2 = 180° - 52° = 128°. questions.solution: When two lines intersect and form four equal angles, each angle must be 90°, which defines perpendicular lines. Perpendicular lines are characterized by forming right angles at their intersection. The other options do not describe lines that form equal angles of 90°.

hi.stem: जब दो रेखाएं एक दूसरे को काटती हैं और चार समान कोण बनाती हैं, तो उन्हें क्या कहा जाता है?

questions.stem: What is the term for two lines that never meet on a plane?
questions.solution: Parallel lines are defined as two lines that never meet on a plane, no matter how far they are extended. Perpendicular lines intersect at a right angle, intersecting lines cross at some point, and transversal refers to a line that intersects two or more other lines.

questions.stem: In the given diagram, lines l and m are intersected by a transversal t. If ∠a is 120° and ∠f is 70°, are lines l and m parallel?
choices: Yes, because the corresponding angles are equal.
No, because the corresponding angles are not equal.

questions.stem: Using the theorem that a line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio, prove that a line through the point of intersection of the diagonals and parallel to the base of a trapezium divides the non-parallel sides in the same ratio. Assume the lines are not parallel
Prove that the triangle is equilateral
Prove that the trapezium is a square
questions.solution: The correct step is to use the properties of parallel lines and transversals, as this helps establish the proportional relationships needed for the proof. The other options are incorrect because assuming lines are not parallel contradicts the given condition, and proving the figure is equilateral or a square is unnecessary and unrelated to the theorem.
